newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Singh asks government to boost reforms.
newsitem.headline: India's Singh asks government to boost reforms.

text.p: Former Indian finance minister Manmohan Singh, whose Congress party offers make-or-break support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition, said on Tuesday the government needed to step up economic reforms.

Singh, architect of a free-market programme launched in 1991 and finance minister for five years until last May, said the coalition must strive to impose fiscal discipline if it was committed to its common minimum programme (CMP) platform.
"Righting a document is one thing. Implementing it in a credible manner is another thing," Singh told the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).
In the CMP, drafted in June, Deve Gowda's 13-party minority coalition pledged to bring down the fiscal deficit to 4.0 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) over the next few years.
The fiscal deficit stood at 5.9 percent in 1995/96 (April-March), and the government aims to reduce it to 5.0 percent in 1996/97.
Singh said Finance Minister P. Chidambaram deserved support in his efforts to reduce the fiscal deficit.
But he gave voice to discontent among businessmen, saying statements on economic management by leading business chambers suggested that "something is amiss".
Singh said the government needed to boost exports and rewrite outdated company and foreign exchange laws that stood in the way of business confidence and foreign investment.

"I was acutely aware that our legal system was a barrier to economic reforms," Singh said. "They have to be modernised so that those who disobey the law are quickly punished and those who are innocent are proved to be innocent."

He did not elaborate, but appeared to be referring to criticism in a section of the industry that law enforcement agents were cracking down on some business houses to implement a socialist foreign exchange law seen as outdated.
"Economic reforms will be incomplete unless legal reforms are carried out," Singh said.
